appraisal_events.evidence: "Oh ! ce n'est pas grave, ce n'est que la septième fois" ... "Il s'est consolé en voulant faire un nouvel enfant à sa femme."
appraisal_events.explanation: The duc waves off the general's repeated electoral defeat and caps it with a wry, faintly risqué remark about his private consolation, deflating the general's misfortune into a running joke rather than treating it as a real setback.

appraisal_events.evidence: le duc qui, ayant dû lui-même renoncer à la politique, aimait assez les insuccès électoraux des autres
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator undercuts the duc's breezy dismissal by exposing its real motive: petty personal envy, since the duc's own political career failed and he now enjoys watching others lose at what he could not pursue.

status_effects.explanation: The general is locally diminished by being turned into an object of casual mockery over his repeated electoral losses and a joking remark about his private life, though the framing ("ce pauvre général") retains some pity rather than pure contempt.
The duc comes off worse because the narrator reveals his nonchalant mockery is really petty schadenfreude rooted in his own abandoned political ambitions.

ambiguities: The 'général' mocked in this passage is never named within the passage itself; he is identified as général de Monserfeuil only by resolving 'ce pauvre général' / 'le général' against the immediately preceding context, and he is not on the reference sheet.

The closing line ('Il s'est consolé en voulant faire un nouvel enfant à sa femme') has no explicit speaker tag; it is read here as a continuation of the duc's mocking remark based on dialogue flow, but the speaker is not stated outright.
